correctness.rationale: Rebuilt cube vertex sign-cut argument: a generic simplex section corresponds to exactly d cube crossing edges, and edge-isoperimetry yields any non-singleton bipartition cuts >=2(d-1)>d, hence only a single vertex can be isolated. For vertex sigma, writing a_i=sigma_i U_i,c_i=1-sigma_i z_i and H=sum c_i a_i gives the strict isolation cone a_i>H/2. Its feasibility with H=1 requires h=1-sum c_i/2>0, so max_sigma <sigma,z>=||z||_1>d-2. Gaussian cones are disjoint up to normal reversal; slice H=1 has parameterization a_i=1/2+h x_i/c_i and Jacobian h^(d-1)||c||/prod c, yielding the displayed exact integral. On diagonal only all-plus sigma occurs; delta=1-d(1-t)/2, uniform integrand convergence gives onset exponent d-1 and coefficient. At d3 independently sampled 70,000 Gaussian normals each t=.2,.5,.8: observed 0,.02511,.15041 versus formula 0,.02470,.15151, consistent but not proof.
